Person period data for discrete time hazard models

Source: R/special-models.R
person_period.Rd

Expands one row per subject into one row per subject and period at risk (Allison 1982; Singer and Willett 2003; Goldstein 2011, ch. 9). The new column event is 1 in the period of the event and 0 otherwise, and period counts the periods. A binary regression of event on period effects and covariates is the discrete time hazard model: the logit link gives the proportional odds model and the cloglog link the grouped proportional hazards model; random effects such as (1 | id) give frailty and multilevel survival models.

Usage

person_period(data, time, status, start = 1)

Arguments

data

Data frame with one row per subject.

time

Name of the column with the last observed period (a positive integer).

status

Name of the column with 1 for an event in period time and 0 for censoring after it.

start

First period (default 1).

Value

The expanded data frame with columns period and event.

Examples

d <- data.frame(id = 1:3, t = c(2, 3, 1), d = c(1, 0, 1), x = c(0.5, -1, 2))
pp <- person_period(d, "t", "d")
pp
#>   id t d    x period event
#> 1  1 2 1  0.5      1     0
#> 2  1 2 1  0.5      2     1
#> 3  2 3 0 -1.0      1     0
#> 4  2 3 0 -1.0      2     0
#> 5  2 3 0 -1.0      3     0
#> 6  3 1 1  2.0      1     1
fit <- regcomp(event ~ factor(period) + x, family = "bernoulli",
               links = list(prob = "cloglog"), data = person_period(
                 data.frame(t = rpois(200, 3) + 1, d = rbinom(200, 1, 0.7),
                            x = rnorm(200)), "t", "d"))
#> Warning: The Hessian is not positive definite; standard errors are unavailable or unreliable.
